tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What did the woman do last Tuesday?

options.A: Met the computer technician.
options.B: Told the man about her trouble.
options.C: Called the man’s company.
options.D: Visited Alpha Maintenance.

questions.cn: 女士上周二做了什么？

optionsCn.A: 见到了电脑技术员。
optionsCn.B: 告诉男士她遇到的麻烦。
optionsCn.C: 给男士所在公司打了电话。
optionsCn.D: 去了一趟阿尔法维修公司。

questions.stem: What does the man say he did when he got the call?

options.A: Consulted someone in charge.
options.B: Came as soon as possible.
options.C: Informed the central office at once.
options.D: Designated an engineer to the case.

questions.cn: 男士说他接到派单后做了什么？

optionsCn.A: 咨询了负责人。
optionsCn.B: 尽快赶来了。
optionsCn.C: 立刻通知了总公司。
optionsCn.D: 指派了一名工程师处理此案。

questions.stem: What is the feeling about the problem around the woman’s workplace?

options.A: Frustration.
options.B: Intimidation.
options.C: Desperation.
options.D: Indignation.

questions.cn: 女士工作场所的人对这个问题的情绪是什么？

optionsCn.A: 沮丧。
optionsCn.B: 畏惧。
optionsCn.C: 绝望。
optionsCn.D: 气愤。

questions.stem: What does the woman say her manager would know?

options.A: Whether the contents have been backed up.
options.B: Whether they can find help somewhere else.
options.C: Whether all data stored on the hard drive has got lost.
options.D: Whether they need to wipe the system directories clean.

questions.cn: 女士说她们经理会知道什么？

optionsCn.A: 内容是否已经备份。
optionsCn.B: 能否在别处找到帮助。
optionsCn.C: 硬盘上存储的所有数据是否已经丢失。
optionsCn.D: 是否需要把系统目录彻底清空。

lines.t: Good morning.
lines.cn: 早上好。

lines.t: My name is Bob Fetterman.
lines.cn: 我叫鲍勃·费特曼。

lines.t: I’m the computer technician.
lines.cn: 我是电脑技术员。

lines.t: Didn’t I call for you last week?
lines.cn: 我上周不是给你打过电话吗？

lines.t: Maybe?
lines.cn: 也许吧？

lines.t: I work for Alpha Maintenance.
lines.cn: 我在阿尔法维修公司工作。

lines.t: I imagine someone from your office called our central office and I’m the engineer designated to your case.
lines.cn: 我猜是你们办公室有人打给我们总公司，我被指派来处理你这个案子。

lines.t: Yeah, I spoke to a lady there last Tuesday, which is now 10 days ago.
lines.cn: 是啊，我上周二和那里的一位女士通过话，到今天已经十天了。

lines.t: I made it clear it was an urgent matter and please send someone as soon as possible.
lines.cn: 我明确说了这是紧急情况，请尽快派人来。

lines.t: Couldn’t you or someone else have come sooner?
lines.cn: 你就不能早点来吗，或者换别人来？

lines.t: I’m sorry, but I’m not in charge of scheduling all logistics.
lines.cn: 抱歉，我并不负责调度所有后勤安排。

lines.t: I simply do not know.
lines.cn: 我确实不知道。

lines.t: All I can tell you is I got the call this week and came as soon as I could.
lines.cn: 我能告诉你的只是：我这周接到派单，就尽快赶来了。

lines.t: I see.
lines.cn: 我明白了。

lines.t: Well, I’ll have you know, my manager is rather indignant that it’s taken you this long to come.
lines.cn: 那我说给你听，我们经理对你们拖了这么久才来相当气愤。

lines.t: I understand it might not be your fault, but nevertheless, you should know what the feeling is around here.
lines.cn: 我理解这可能不是你的错，但你还是该知道这边的人是什么情绪。

lines.t: I understand, and I’m sorry for any inconvenience.
lines.cn: 我理解，给你们带来不便我很抱歉。

lines.t: I will try to resolve your computer problem as swiftly and optimally as I can.
lines.cn: 我会尽可能迅速、妥善地解决你的电脑问题。

lines.t: What and where is the issue?
lines.cn: 问题是什么，在哪儿？

lines.t: It’s this machine right here.
lines.cn: 就是这台机器。

lines.t: It was running slow for a while, I guess, and gradually got worse and worse.
lines.cn: 它有一阵子运行很慢，我想，后来渐渐越来越糟。

lines.t: Last Tuesday, it just stopped working altogether.
lines.cn: 上周二，它干脆完全罢工了。

lines.t: If you switch it on, you will see what I mean.
lines.cn: 你开机看看就明白我的意思了。

lines.t: Okay.
lines.cn: 好。

lines.t: Do you know if it’s backed up?
lines.cn: 你知道它有没有备份吗？

lines.t: Backed up?
lines.cn: 备份？

lines.t: I mean, do you know if its contents have been copied and saved somewhere else?
lines.cn: 我是说，你知道它的内容有没有被复制、保存到别处吗？

lines.t: I don’t know.
lines.cn: 我不知道。

lines.t: Well, depending on the ensuing operative scenario, if I need to wipe the system directories clean in order to reconfigure default protocols,
lines.cn: 嗯，视接下来实际操作的情形而定，如果我需要把系统目录彻底清空、重新配置默认协议，

lines.t: then my first intervention should be to intricately retrieve all inventories that I can.
lines.cn: 那我首先要做的就是尽可能细致地抢救出所有资料。

lines.t: Otherwise, all data that was stored on its hard drive will be forever lost.
lines.cn: 否则，硬盘上存储的所有数据都会永久丢失。

lines.t: My manager would know.
lines.cn: 我们经理会知道。

lines.t: Let me go get him.
lines.cn: 我去把他叫来。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What will many people say about a career in law?

options.A: It’s boring.
options.B: It’s challenging.
options.C: It’s a beautiful thing.
options.D: It’s unlike most jobs.

questions.cn: 许多人会怎样评价法律这一职业？

optionsCn.A: 很无聊。
optionsCn.B: 很有挑战性。
optionsCn.C: 是件美好的事。
optionsCn.D: 与大多数工作不同。

questions.stem: What does the man say most of his work involves?

options.A: Arbitrating between disagreeing solicitors.
options.B: Preventing disputes from escalating.
options.C: Buying and selling property.
options.D: Mediating land disputes.

questions.cn: 男士说他大部分工作涉及什么？

optionsCn.A: 在有分歧的律师之间仲裁。
optionsCn.B: 防止纠纷升级。
optionsCn.C: 买卖房产。
optionsCn.D: 调解土地纠纷。

questions.stem: Why does the man say it’s usually better to resolve problems outside of court whenever possible?

options.A: Courts are intended for fixing major legal disputes.
options.B: Courts are getting too bureaucratic to function.
options.C: Courts can be frustrating and expensive.
options.D: Courts can be frightening and arbitrary.

questions.cn: 男士为什么说只要能庭外解决就更好？

optionsCn.A: 法院是为解决重大法律纠纷而设的。
optionsCn.B: 法院官僚化到无法运作。
optionsCn.C: 法院可能令人沮丧而且花钱。
optionsCn.D: 法院可能令人恐惧且任意专断。

questions.stem: What does the man think is required of any law professional?

options.A: The ability to make arguments in a unique way.
options.B: The skill of preventing conflicts between parties concerned.
options.C: The skill of foreseeing any potential stakes in their work.
options.D: The ability to express themselves clearly and forcefully.

questions.cn: 男士认为任何法律从业者都需要什么？

optionsCn.A: 以独特方式提出论证的能力。
optionsCn.B: 防止有关各方之间发生冲突的技巧。
optionsCn.C: 预见工作中任何潜在风险的技巧。
optionsCn.D: 清晰有力地表达自己的能力。

lines.t: Have you given more thought to studying law?
lines.cn: 学法律这件事，你又多考虑过了吗？

lines.t: I’ve been thinking about it a lot, yes.
lines.cn: 是的，我想了很多。

lines.t: In fact, this is why I wished to speak to you.
lines.cn: 其实，这正是我想找你聊的原因。

lines.t: I wanted to hear more about what it’s like.
lines.cn: 我想多听听这行到底是什么样。

lines.t: A career in law is a beautiful thing in my opinion.
lines.cn: 在我看来，从事法律是一份很美好的职业。

lines.t: Many people will say it’s a boring field, but I disagree.
lines.cn: 很多人会说这行很无聊，但我不同意。

lines.t: The thing is there are many different branches of law and many different jobs.
lines.cn: 问题在于，法律有许多不同的分支，也有许多不同的岗位。

lines.t: You are involved with buildings and construction, right?
lines.cn: 你打交道的是建筑和工程建设，对吧？

lines.t: Correct.
lines.cn: 没错。

lines.t: I’m a solicitor, specializing in real estate.
lines.cn: 我是一名事务律师，专攻房地产。

lines.t: Most of my work involves mediating land disputes.
lines.cn: 我的工作大多是调解土地纠纷。

lines.t: Do you mind giving me an example?
lines.cn: 能给我举个例子吗？

lines.t: Sure.
lines.cn: 当然。

lines.t: So in many cases I am employed to arbitrate between two clashing parties.
lines.cn: 很多情况下，我受托在激烈对立的两方之间进行仲裁。

lines.t: Let’s say for example, there are two landowners who are in a thorny disagreement about something like the borders of their adjacent plots.
lines.cn: 比如说，两位土地所有者因为相邻地块的边界之类的问题陷入棘手争执。

lines.t: Someone may employ me to break the deadlock and resolve the dispute.
lines.cn: 有人可能雇用我打破僵局、解决争端。

lines.t: Often my work involves negotiating agreements, plain and simple.
lines.cn: 我的工作常常就是谈判达成协议，就这么简单。

lines.t: So you are saying that a lot of what you do is fix people’s legal issues, like you try to find a solution that benefits everyone and that prevents a problem from escalating.
lines.cn: 所以你的意思是，你做的很多事是解决人们的法律问题，比如努力找出既让各方受益、又能防止问题升级的方案。

lines.t: Exactly, well put.
lines.cn: 正是，说得好。

lines.t: You need to remember that courts, like all bureaucracies really, can be very messy, frustrating, and expensive.
lines.cn: 你要记住，法院和所有官僚机构一样，可能非常混乱、令人沮丧，而且花钱。

lines.t: For this reason, it’s usually better to resolve problems outside of court whenever possible.
lines.cn: 正因如此，只要能庭外解决，通常就更好。

lines.t: I see.
lines.cn: 我明白了。

lines.t: So besides knowing the law inside out, you need good people skills, right?
lines.cn: 所以除了把法律吃透，还得有很好的人际交往能力，对吧？

lines.t: Of course.
lines.cn: 当然。

lines.t: Any job that involves people requires good interpersonal skills, and any law professional needs to be very eloquent at articulating that argument.
lines.cn: 任何与人打交道的工作都需要良好的人际技能，而任何法律从业者都必须非常善于清晰地表达论证。

lines.t: Right.
lines.cn: 对。

lines.t: So I’ve been thinking about studying criminal law.
lines.cn: 所以我一直在考虑学刑法。

lines.t: I think it sounds very interesting.
lines.cn: 我觉得那听起来很有意思。

lines.t: Mm-hmm, yes.
lines.cn: 嗯嗯，是的。

lines.t: I’d say there’s more money in property law, but the stakes are higher in criminal law.
lines.cn: 要我说，房地产业务赚得更多，但刑法牵涉的风险更大。

lines.t: I can see how you would find it more interesting.
lines.cn: 我看得出你为什么会觉得它更有意思。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What did the researchers do in their review in the journal Trends in Cognitive Sciences?

options.A: They looked into the relationship between one’s prior knowledge and creativity.
options.B: They offered novel ways to help older adults to keep their memories from aging.
options.C: They proposed an explanation for old people’s difficulty in retrieving memories.
options.D: They advanced a new model concerning human information storage and retrieval.

questions.cn: 研究者在《认知科学趋势》期刊的这篇综述中做了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们研究了一个人既有知识与创造力之间的关系。
optionsCn.B: 他们提出了帮助老年人防止记忆衰老的新方法。
optionsCn.C: 他们为老年人提取记忆困难提出了解释。
optionsCn.D: 他们就人类信息存储与提取提出了新模型。

questions.stem: What do several behavioral and brain imaging studies show?

options.A: Young adults rely on memory while older adults keep notes as a reminder.
options.B: Older adults often retrieve irrelevant memories along with what they want.
options.C: Young adults accumulate knowledge much more quickly than older adults.
options.D: Older adults generally perform cognitive tasks much slower than young adults.

questions.cn: 多项行为学与脑成像研究显示了什么？

optionsCn.A: 年轻人靠记忆，而老年人靠记笔记提醒自己。
optionsCn.B: 老年人常常把不相关的记忆连同想要的记忆一并提取出来。
optionsCn.C: 年轻人积累知识的速度比老年人快得多。
optionsCn.D: 老年人完成认知任务通常比年轻人慢得多。

questions.stem: What does evidence suggest regarding older adults?

options.A: They show preserved, and sometimes enhanced, creativity.
options.B: They frequently suffer from disorderly crowded memories.
options.C: They can rely on their accumulated wisdom in an emergency.
options.D: They may well be served by forgetting their prior knowledge.

questions.cn: 关于老年人，证据表明了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们的创造力得以保留，有时甚至增强。
optionsCn.B: 他们常常被杂乱拥挤的记忆所困扰。
optionsCn.C: 他们在紧急情况下可以依靠积累的智慧。
optionsCn.D: 忘掉既有知识对他们可能反而有益。

lines.t: When a person tries to access a memory, their brains quickly examine everything stored in it to find the relevant information.
lines.cn: 当一个人试图调取一段记忆时，大脑会迅速检视其中储存的一切，以找到相关信息。

lines.t: But as we age, many of us have difficulty retrieving memories.
lines.cn: 但随着年龄增长，我们许多人提取记忆变得困难。

lines.t: In a review published in the journal Trends in Cognitive Sciences on February 11th, researchers propose an explanation for why this might be happening: the brains of older adults allocate more space to accumulated knowledge and have more material to navigate when attempting to access memories.
lines.cn: 在 2 月 11 日发表于《认知科学趋势》期刊的一篇综述中，研究者对这种现象提出了解释：老年人的大脑把更多空间分配给积累的知识，因此在调取记忆时需要检索的材料也更多。

lines.t: While this wealth of prior knowledge can make memory retrieval challenging, the researchers say it has its upsides-this life experience can aid with creativity and decision-making.
lines.cn: 研究者说，尽管如此丰厚的既有知识会让记忆提取变得困难，它也有好处——这些人生经验有助于创造力和决策。

lines.t: Researchers Tarek Amer, Jordana Wynn and Lynn Hasher looked at several behavioral and brain imaging studies, which show that older adults have difficulty suppressing information that is no longer relevant and that when searching for a specific memory, they often retrieve other, irrelevant memories along with it.
lines.cn: 研究者塔里克·阿梅尔、乔丹娜·温恩和林恩·哈舍尔考察了多项行为学与脑成像研究，这些研究显示：老年人难以抑制不再相关的信息；在搜寻某段特定记忆时，他们常常把其他不相关的记忆一并带出。

lines.t: The studies also showed that when given a cognitive task, older adults rely more heavily on previous knowledge than younger adults do.
lines.cn: 这些研究还显示，面对认知任务时，老年人比年轻人更依赖既有知识。

lines.t: While the researchers focus primarily on the difficulties that these disorderly, crowded memories may pose, they also highlight a few situations in which these same memory patterns may be useful.
lines.cn: 尽管研究者主要关注这些杂乱、拥挤的记忆可能带来的困难，他们也指出了一些同样的记忆模式可能有用的情况。

lines.t: Evidence suggests that older adults show preserved, and at times enhanced, creativity as a function of enriched memories, the researchers write.
lines.cn: 研究者写道，有证据表明，老年人的创造力因记忆的丰富而得以保留，有时甚至增强。

lines.t: They further hypothesize that older adults may be well served by their prior knowledge when it comes to decision-making, where they can pull on their accumulated wisdom.
lines.cn: 他们进一步推测，在决策方面，老年人凭借积累的智慧，其既有知识可能对他们很有帮助。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 4 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn about American workers from the passage?

options.A: They are actually proud of the goods and services they produce.
options.B: They are worried about being alienated from the outside world.
options.C: They are rarely in control of many things related to their work.
options.D: They are longing to share the profits made from their work.

questions.cn: 从文章中我们了解到美国工人的什么情况？

optionsCn.A: 他们其实为自己生产的产品和服务感到自豪。
optionsCn.B: 他们担心自己被外部世界疏远。
optionsCn.C: 他们很少能掌控与工作相关的许多事情。
optionsCn.D: 他们渴望分享自己劳动创造的利润。

questions.stem: What does the passage say long working hours contribute to?

options.A: The steady decrease in productivity.
options.B: The adverse effect on physical health.
options.C: The feeling of being time poor.
options.D: The rising economic inequality.

questions.cn: 文章说长时间工作导致了什么？

optionsCn.A: 生产率的持续下降。
optionsCn.B: 对身体健康的不良影响。
optionsCn.C: 时间匮乏感。
optionsCn.D: 经济不平等的加剧。

questions.stem: What does automation do, according to the passage?

options.A: It alters the structure of work.
options.B: It puts jobs and wages at risk.
options.C: It liberates people from tedious and laborious work.
options.D: It creates new work opportunities in the IT industry.

questions.cn: 根据文章，自动化做了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它改变了工作结构。
optionsCn.B: 它使工作和工资面临风险。
optionsCn.C: 它把人从繁琐劳累的工作中解放出来。
optionsCn.D: 它在 IT 行业创造了新的工作机会。

questions.stem: What do post-work theorists advocate?

options.A: Finding meaning in work.
options.B: Prioritizing life over work.
options.C: Improving relationships in the community.
options.D: Realizing one’s social value in the workplace.

questions.cn: 后工作理论家主张什么？

optionsCn.A: 在工作中寻找意义。
optionsCn.B: 把生活置于工作之上。
optionsCn.C: 改善社区中的人际关系。
optionsCn.D: 在工作场所实现个人社会价值。

lines.t: There are at least four major problems with work in America today.
lines.cn: 如今美国的工作至少存在四个重大问题。

lines.t: First, work can be alienating.
lines.cn: 第一，工作可能使人异化。

lines.t: Workers are often not in control of how they work, when they work, what is done with the goods and services they produce, and what is done with the profits made from their work.
lines.cn: 工人往往无法决定自己如何工作、何时工作、自己生产的产品和服务被如何使用，以及自己劳动带来的利润被如何处置。

lines.t: Second, workers are not paid the full value of their labor.
lines.cn: 第二，工人没有拿到其劳动的全部价值。

lines.t: Real wages have not kept pace with productivity, driving economic inequality and a decline in labor’s share of income.
lines.cn: 实际工资没有跟上生产率的增长，导致经济不平等加剧、劳动收入份额下降。

lines.t: Third, people are time poor.
lines.cn: 第三，人们时间匮乏。

lines.t: In the U.S., full-time employees work an average of 8.72 hours per day despite productivity increases.
lines.cn: 在美国，尽管生产率提高了，全职员工平均每天工作 8.72 小时。

lines.t: Long working hours contribute to the feeling of “time poverty”, which has an adverse effect on psychological well-being.
lines.cn: 长时间工作加剧了“时间贫困”感，对心理健康造成不良影响。

lines.t: Fourth, automation puts jobs and wages at risk.
lines.cn: 第四，自动化使工作和工资面临风险。

lines.t: Technological innovation could in theory liberate people from the 40-hour work week.
lines.cn: 技术创新理论上能把人从每周 40 小时工作中解放出来。

lines.t: But unless changes are made to the structure of work, automation will simply exert downward pressure on wages and further diminish work opportunities.
lines.cn: 但除非工作结构发生改变，自动化只会对工资形成下行压力，并进一步减少工作机会。

lines.t: So, what can be done to alleviate these problems?
lines.cn: 那么，能做些什么来缓解这些问题？

lines.t: There are competing visions of the best way to arrive at a solution.
lines.cn: 至于最好的解决路径是什么，存在着相互竞争的不同设想。

lines.t: One vision is what’s known as the “post-work” position.
lines.cn: 其中一种是所谓的“后工作”立场。

lines.t: The post-work theorists believe that work should not hold a central position in our lives or take up so much of our time.
lines.cn: 后工作理论家认为，工作不应在我们的生活中占据中心位置，也不该占用我们那么多时间。

lines.t: They assert that although doing some work might be necessary, meaning, purpose and social value reside in the communities and relationships built and sustained outside of the workplace.
lines.cn: 他们断言，尽管做一些工作或许是必要的，但意义、目的和社会价值存在于工作场所之外建立和维系的各种群体与关系之中。

lines.t: Thus, life should be seen as an end in itself.
lines.cn: 因此，生活本身应当被视为目的。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 5 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say even our personal beliefs about effort can do?

options.A: Affect our attitude to novel tasks.
options.B: Distinguish us in the social world.
options.C: Outweigh IQ in importance.
options.D: Impact academic achievements.

questions.cn: 讲话者说，甚至我们对努力的个人信念也能怎样？

optionsCn.A: 影响我们对新任务的态度。
optionsCn.B: 让我们在社会世界中显得与众不同。
optionsCn.C: 在重要性上超过智商。
optionsCn.D: 影响学业成绩。

questions.stem: How did the researchers turn on the music toy in their experiment?

options.A: By pressing a hidden button.
options.B: By pushing a big button on top.
options.C: By pressing two buttons at the same time.
options.D: By helping the babies push the right button.

questions.cn: 研究者是如何打开实验中的音乐玩具的？

optionsCn.A: 按一个隐藏的按钮。
optionsCn.B: 按顶部的大按钮。
optionsCn.C: 同时按两个按钮。
optionsCn.D: 帮婴儿按下正确的按钮。

questions.stem: What could the infants do in the experiment according to the speaker?

options.A: Perform difficult tasks successfully just by observing how adults acted.
options.B: Make generalizable inferences about persistence from a few examples.
options.C: Adapt themselves to different social contexts.
options.D: Work hard to interact with experimenters.

questions.cn: 根据讲话者，婴儿在实验中能做什么？

optionsCn.A: 仅通过观察成年人怎么做就能成功完成困难任务。
optionsCn.B: 从几个例子中就对“坚持”做出可推广的推断。
optionsCn.C: 使自己适应不同的社会情境。
optionsCn.D: 努力与实验者互动。

lines.t: Recent studies show that self-control and persistence increase academic outcomes, independent of IQ.
lines.cn: 近期研究显示，自控力和坚持能提升学业成绩，且与智商无关。

lines.t: Even our personal beliefs about efforts can affect academic outcomes.
lines.cn: 甚至我们对努力的个人信念也会影响学业成绩。

lines.t: Children who think effort leads to achievement outperform those who believe ability is a fixed trait.
lines.cn: 认为努力带来成就的孩子，表现优于那些认为能力是固定特质的孩子。

lines.t: Given the link between persistence and academic success, decisions about efforts are particularly important in childhood.
lines.cn: 鉴于坚持与学业成功之间的关联，在童年时期，关于是否付出努力的判断尤为重要。

lines.t: Yet, relatively little research has explored how young children learn what’s worth the effort.
lines.cn: 然而，相对少有研究探讨幼儿是如何学会判断什么值得付出努力的。

lines.t: We all know that infants are keen observers of the social world, but they’re not just idly watching; they are tiny learning machines.
lines.cn: 我们都知道婴儿是社会世界的敏锐观察者，但他们并非只是无所事事地看着；他们是小小的学习机器。

lines.t: They can generalize such abstract concepts as causal relationships and social roles from just a few examples.
lines.cn: 仅凭几个例子，他们就能概括出因果关系、社会角色等抽象概念。

lines.t: Even a 15-month-old infant can outperform a high-level computer in such tasks.
lines.cn: 在这类任务上，甚至 15 个月大的婴儿也能胜过高级计算机。

lines.t: Could infants also make broad generalizable inferences from a few examples when it comes to effort?
lines.cn: 那么在“努力”这件事上，婴儿是否也能从几个例子中做出宽泛可推广的推断？

lines.t: If so, then maybe persistence isn’t simply a character trait.
lines.cn: 如果是，那么坚持也许并不只是一种性格特质。

lines.t: Maybe it’s flexible and adaptable based on social context.
lines.cn: 也许它是灵活的、可依据社会情境调整的。

lines.t: To explore this question, we showed 15-month-old babies one of two things-an experimenter working hard to achieve two different goals, or an experimenter who effortlessly reached each goal.
lines.cn: 为探究这个问题，我们给 15 个月大的婴儿看两种情况之一：一位实验者努力尝试、最终达成两个不同目标；或一位实验者毫不费力地达到每个目标。

lines.t: Then we introduced the baby to a novel music toy that seemed as if it could be activated by pushing a big button on top.
lines.cn: 随后我们给婴儿介绍了一个新奇的音乐玩具，它看起来似乎按一下顶部的大按钮就能启动。

lines.t: The button could be pressed down, but didn’t actually activate anything.
lines.cn: 那个按钮能按下去，但实际上什么也启动不了。

lines.t: Out of sight of the babies, we turned on the music toy with a hidden button so that they heard the toy making music.
lines.cn: 在婴儿看不见的地方，我们用隐藏的按钮打开了音乐玩具，让他们听到玩具在放音乐。

lines.t: We gave the babies the music toy and left the room.
lines.cn: 我们把音乐玩具交给婴儿，然后离开了房间。

lines.t: Then analysts who didn’t know which condition each baby was in, watched video tapes of the experiment and counted how many times babies tried to activate the toy by pressing the button.
lines.cn: 随后，不知道每个婴儿属于哪个组别的分析人员观看实验录像，统计婴儿按按钮试图启动玩具的次数。

lines.t: Across one study and a pre-registered duplication, babies who had seen an adult persist and succeed pushed the button about twice as many times as those who saw an adult effortlessly succeed.
lines.cn: 在一项研究及一次预注册的重复实验中，看过成年人坚持不懈并取得成功的婴儿，按按钮的次数约为看过成年人毫不费力就成功的婴儿的两倍。

lines.t: In other words, babies learned that effort was valuable after watching just two examples of an adult working hard and succeeding.
lines.cn: 换句话说，仅仅看过两个成年人努力并成功的例子，婴儿就学到了努力是有价值的。

lines.t: Part of what’s exciting about this finding is that the babies didn’t just imitate the adult’s actions.
lines.cn: 这一发现令人兴奋的一点在于，婴儿并不只是模仿成人的动作。

lines.t: Instead, they generalized the value of effort to a novel task.
lines.cn: 他们反而把努力的价值推广到了一个新任务上。

lines.t: The experimenter never demonstrated pushing a button or trying to make music.
lines.cn: 实验者从未示范过按按钮或尝试让音乐响起。

lines.t: Instead, the babies learned from different examples of effortful actions that the new toy probably also required persistence.
lines.cn: 婴儿是从不同的“努力行为”例子中推断出：这个新玩具大概也需要坚持不懈。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 6 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What is the speaker’s purpose of giving this talk?

options.A: Offering advice on overcoming habitual lateness.
options.B: Exemplifying various recreational opportunities.
options.C: Scrutinizing individuals’ defining traits.
options.D: Suggesting ways for setting priorities.

questions.cn: 讲话者做这次演讲的目的是什么？

optionsCn.A: 就克服习惯性迟到给出建议。
optionsCn.B: 举例说明各种休闲机会。
optionsCn.C: 审视个人的显著特征。
optionsCn.D: 提出确定优先事项的方法。

questions.stem: What should you do if mornings are a struggle for you?

options.A: Make the breakfast simpler.
options.B: Take the alarms seriously.
options.C: Ready yourself in the early dawn.
options.D: Get prepared the night before.

questions.cn: 如果早晨对你来说很吃力，你应该怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 把早餐弄简单些。
optionsCn.B: 认真对待闹钟。
optionsCn.C: 天不亮就起床准备。
optionsCn.D: 前一晚就做好准备。

questions.stem: According to the speaker, what can we do to combat unexpected delays?

options.A: Finish the prior task 30 minutes earlier.
options.B: Keep ourselves from hitting a bump.
options.C: Leave time in between activities.
options.D: Try to avoid possible hold-ups.

questions.cn: 根据讲话者，我们能做什么来应对意外延误？

optionsCn.A: 提前 30 分钟完成前一项任务。
optionsCn.B: 让自己不碰上状况。
optionsCn.C: 在活动之间留出时间。
optionsCn.D: 尽量避免可能的耽搁。

lines.t: If chronic lateness has taken over your life and turned into a defining trait of who you are, it’s likely that you’re losing out on job offers, recreational opportunities, friendships, and more.
lines.cn: 如果习惯性迟到已经占据你的生活、成为你身上一个显著标签，那么你很可能会失去工作机会、休闲机会、友谊等等。

lines.t: If you are showing up late to your own life, get organized, prioritize punctuality, and address any underlying causes.
lines.cn: 如果你在自己的人生里都迟到，那就把事情安排起来，把守时放在优先位置，并解决任何深层原因。

lines.t: When you have to be somewhere, try to arrive 15 to 30 minutes before you need to.
lines.cn: 当你必须到某个地方时，尽量提前 15 到 30 分钟到达。

lines.t: If you always run late, that means you must be failing to account for something you always do.
lines.cn: 如果你总是迟到，那就说明你必定忽略了某件你每次都会做的事。

lines.t: Anticipate that by giving yourself extra time to arrive.
lines.cn: 预见到这一点，就给自己留出额外的时间。

lines.t: Keep track of whether or not you actually do arrive early.
lines.cn: 留意自己是否真的提前到了。

lines.t: You might find that leaving early gets you to places exactly on time.
lines.cn: 你可能会发现，早点出门反而正好让你准时到达。

lines.t: Set two alarms.
lines.cn: 定两个闹钟。

lines.t: Set one alarm that lets you know it’s time to drop what you’re doing and a second alarm that means you need to walk out the door.
lines.cn: 一个提醒你该放下手头的事，第二个提醒你必须出门了。

lines.t: Obey the alarms.
lines.cn: 遵从闹钟。

lines.t: As soon as the first alarm goes off, stop what you’re doing.
lines.cn: 第一个闹钟一响，就停下手里的活。

lines.t: If it’s something you’ll be coming back to, like a project for work, make a note to remind yourself where you left off.
lines.cn: 如果那是你之后还要接着做的事，比如工作项目，就记一下自己做到哪儿了。

lines.t: Grab everything you need and make sure you know how to get where you’re going.
lines.cn: 拿上所有需要的东西，并确认自己知道怎么去目的地。

lines.t: Aim to be out the door and on your way before the second alarm rings.
lines.cn: 争取在第二个闹钟响之前就出了门、上了路。

lines.t: This will only work if you take the alarms seriously, so make sure you react as soon as you hear them.
lines.cn: 只有你认真对待闹钟，这招才管用，所以听到就要立刻行动。

lines.t: Prepare for the day ahead.
lines.cn: 提前为第二天做准备。

lines.t: Have all of your notes and materials organized well in advance of each event, so that all you have to do is grab them and go when it’s the actual day.
lines.cn: 在每次活动之前，就把所有笔记和材料整理好，这样到了当天你只需拿上就走。

lines.t: If mornings are a struggle for you, do as much as you can to ready yourself the night before.
lines.cn: 如果早晨对你来说很吃力，就尽量在前一晚把一切都准备好。

lines.t: Before you go to bed, lay out your clothes and pack your bag for the next day.
lines.cn: 睡前把衣服摆好、把包收拾好。

lines.t: Learn to leave time in between tasks and meetings.
lines.cn: 学会在任务和会议之间留出时间。

lines.t: It soon becomes unbearable to shift between one meeting and another without space in between.
lines.cn: 在一个会议和下一个会议之间没有间隙地来回切换，很快就会让人受不了。

lines.t: If you overschedule yourself, however, you’ll arrive late as soon as you hit a bump.
lines.cn: 不过，如果你把日程排得过满，一旦出点状况你就会迟到。

lines.t: As well as giving you space, this time also acts as a buffer between events, which can be borrowed from, should you be held up in a prior meeting, allowing you to still get to the next one on time.
lines.cn: 这段时间不仅给你留出余地，还在各项活动之间起到缓冲作用：万一前一个会拖住了你，还可以从缓冲里挪用，让你仍能准时赶到下一个。

lines.t: Calculate transit time between activities and then add 10 to 30 minutes for unexpected delays.
lines.cn: 估算活动之间的通行时间，再额外加上 10 到 30 分钟应对意外延误。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 7 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do visitors find about the cities they’ve been to?

options.A: Their lifestyles vary.
options.B: Their traits vary.
options.C: They have different customs.
options.D: They have different feels.

questions.cn: 访客对他们去过的城市有什么发现？

optionsCn.A: 他们的生活方式各不相同。
optionsCn.B: 他们的特征各不相同。
optionsCn.C: 他们有不同的习俗。
optionsCn.D: 他们给人不同的感受。

questions.stem: What did one study find about Bostonians compared with residents of other U.S. cities?

options.A: They are not as willing to help strangers.
options.B: They are not as patient with one another.
options.C: They violate traffic rules more frequently.
options.D: They become more easily irritated in public.

questions.cn: 一项研究就波士顿人与美国其他城市居民的比较发现了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们不那么愿意帮助陌生人。
optionsCn.B: 他们彼此之间不那么有耐心。
optionsCn.C: 他们更频繁地违反交通规则。
optionsCn.D: 他们在公共场合更容易发火。

questions.stem: What does Thomas O’Connor say about the idea of strangers greeting one another?

options.A: It was practiced by Boston’s founding fathers.
options.B: It is not deemed exotic by Proper Bostonians.
options.C: It was adopted by Boston’s upper class.
options.D: It is not part of Boston’s local culture.

questions.cn: 关于陌生人互相问候这一想法，托马斯·奥康纳说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 波士顿的先辈们实践过这一做法。
optionsCn.B: 正宗波士顿人并不觉得它异乎寻常。
optionsCn.C: 它被波士顿的上层阶级采纳了。
optionsCn.D: 它不属于波士顿的当地文化。

questions.stem: What does the speaker think Boston should do?

options.A: Stick to its own way of showing courtesy to strangers.
options.B: Follow the examples set by Paris and New York City.
options.C: Learn from the world’s major cities in promoting tourism.
options.D: Take pride in its history and adhere to its cultural tradition.

questions.cn: 讲话者认为波士顿应该怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 坚持自己向陌生人表示礼貌的方式。
optionsCn.B: 效仿巴黎和纽约市的做法。
optionsCn.C: 在发展旅游业上向世界大城市学习。
optionsCn.D: 为自身历史自豪并恪守文化传统。

lines.t: Do you think Bostonians put out the welcome mat?
lines.cn: 你觉得波士顿人热情好客吗？

lines.t: Do you find other cities to be more or less polite?
lines.cn: 你觉得其他城市是更礼貌还是更不礼貌？

lines.t: Different cities have different feels for visitors.
lines.cn: 不同的城市给访客的感受不同。

lines.t: Some are friendly and open; some are formal and distant.
lines.cn: 有些友好开放；有些拘谨疏远。

lines.t: Boston tends to seem hurried and sometimes a little rude.
lines.cn: 波士顿往往显得行色匆匆，有时还有点粗鲁。

lines.t: That’s what some tourists have said.
lines.cn: 这是一些游客的说法。

lines.t: One study found that people here are less willing to volunteer to help strangers than those residents of other U.S. cities.
lines.cn: 一项研究发现，这里的人比美国其他城市的居民更不愿意主动帮助陌生人。

lines.t: Take a close look next time you’re in Boston, and here are some of the things you’ll probably see:
lines.cn: 下次到波士顿时仔细看看，你很可能会看到这样一些景象：

lines.t: people smoking in the subway stations despite the frequent reminders not to do so;
lines.cn: 尽管反复提醒不要吸烟，仍有人在地铁站里抽烟；

lines.t: pedestrians walking when the crosswalk lights say not to do so, ignoring the cars;
lines.cn: 人行横道灯显示禁止通行时，行人照样穿过，无视车辆；

lines.t: car drivers speeding, making a loud noise with the horn and occasionally cursing at each other.
lines.cn: 汽车司机超速行驶，喇叭按得震天响，偶尔还互相骂上几句。

lines.t: Drivers who can’t be bothered to find a place to park, but instead simply turn on their blinker and stop in the middle of the street.
lines.cn: 有些司机懒得找车位，干脆打开转向灯，把车停在马路中间。

lines.t: Sometimes Bostonians seem like they’re just too busy to be polite.
lines.cn: 有时波士顿人看起来就是忙得顾不上礼貌。

lines.t: Why is their city like that?
lines.cn: 这座城市为什么会这样？

lines.t: Former U.S. representative Chester Atkins says it’s because the Puritan founding fathers were themselves impatient and bad-tempered, and had little time for courtesy.
lines.cn: 前美国众议员切斯特·阿特金斯说，这是因为清教徒先辈们本身就急躁、脾气坏，没多少工夫讲礼貌。

lines.t: That culture has carried down to the present day, he believes.
lines.cn: 他认为，这种文化一直延续到今天。

lines.t: Boston College professor Thomas O’Connor thinks a contributing factor is Boston’s history as a city where each new group of immigrants was treated with suspicion and exclusion.
lines.cn: 波士顿学院教授托马斯·奥康纳认为，一个促成因素是波士顿的历史：每一批新移民都曾遭到猜疑和排斥。

lines.t: That’s given Boston a sense of clannishness and reserve, he thinks.
lines.cn: 他认为，这给波士顿带来了一种抱团排外和矜持的气质。

lines.t: The idea of a stranger greeting another stranger is simply not part of the local culture, he says.
lines.cn: 他说，陌生人向陌生人打招呼这种想法，根本不属于当地文化的一部分。

lines.t: People will begin a conversation with someone they know, but not with a stranger.
lines.cn: 人们会和熟人攀谈，但不会和陌生人攀谈。

lines.t: Ralph Whitehead, a professor of journalism at the University of Massachusetts at Amherst, thinks it’s because Boston’s upper class used manners to make class distinctions.
lines.cn: 马萨诸塞大学阿默斯特分校新闻学教授拉尔夫·怀特黑德则认为，这是因为波士顿的上层阶级用礼仪来划分阶级界限。

lines.t: By being snobbish about manners, Proper Bostonians made other people scornful of courtesy, he says.
lines.cn: 他说，正宗的波士顿人用势利的礼仪姿态，让其他人对礼貌本身都心生鄙夷。

lines.t: Some say that’s just the way Boston is and that the city will never change.
lines.cn: 有人说波士顿就是这样，这座城市永远不会变。

lines.t: Still, other cities with reputations for worse rudeness are trying hard to change their images.
lines.cn: 但其他以更粗鲁著称的城市正在努力改变形象。

lines.t: Paris is one example where people are trying to be friendly.
lines.cn: 巴黎就是一个例子，那里的人们正努力变得友善。

lines.t: New York City is another.
lines.cn: 纽约市是另一个。

lines.t: There, the city is trying to persuade subway riders to be more considerate.
lines.cn: 在那里，市政府正设法劝导地铁乘客多替他人着想。

lines.t: If those cities can make the effort, maybe Boston should as well.
lines.cn: 如果那些城市都能做出努力，也许波士顿也该如此。
